about: Every place in src/main that makes a synchronous file call (anything ending in Sync) or creates a process
(child_process spawn/exec/execFile/fork and their Sync forms, electron utilityProcess.fork, node-pty spawn).
tests/electron/mainThreadScan.test.ts scans src/main and fails when a site is not listed here, and when a listed
site is gone or has fewer calls (so this list only ever shrinks by being fixed). One line per site, sorted.
Why this exists: node-pty runs inside the Electron main process, so every keystroke and every echo passes through
the main thread; one synchronous file call or one spawn there can freeze every terminal (on a busy Windows laptop
with Defender: 0.1 s to 1.5 s each). The hot paths (a keystroke, a submit, PTY output, a file-system watcher event,
a steady-state timer tick, opening or closing a terminal) must not appear below. Their work goes to the proc host,
a worker, or fs.promises through src/main/offMainFiles.ts (bounded concurrency, bounded queue).
A new entry needs a tag and a one-line reason. Do not add an entry for a site that a keystroke, a watcher event,
a timer or PTY output can reach: move the work instead.

tags.startup: runs once while the app starts, before the first terminal exists (or a lazy init that start-up already made)
tags.user-action: runs because the user asked for it (a click, a save, a setting, a pick), never on a typing, watcher or timer path
tags.off-main: runs in another process or thread (memory host, Headroom proxy, embed worker), not on the main thread
tags.fallback: degraded path only: the proc host is down and the call runs in process rather than not at all
tags.rare: runs on a rare event (a crashed host), a few bytes, never steady-state
tags.lane-c: owned by the memory lane (fix/typing154c); that lane removes the entry when it moves the work
